watchdog_ngos_searched: Democracy for the Arab World Now (DAWN)
adversarial_framing_check_finding: Applicable: the ongoing Houthi/Red Sea security story names Saudi Arabia in a geopolitical/security context. Checked Al Jazeera (framed Saudi as victim, no adversarial framing in-window), Middle East Eye (no in-window piece located), and Iranian state media (Press TV) which carried explicit Saudi-as-aggressor/oppressor framing on 2026-09-25 (Grand Mufti/Yanbu deployment; UNICEF Yemen displacement). Press TV items were NOT used: Negative Articles was already populated with credible non-state-aligned outlets, the France/Yanbu event they reframe was covered in the 25 Sep edition, and foregrounding Iranian state propaganda in a Saudi government deliverable is itself reputationally inadvisable. The check was nonetheless genuinely run and recorded here.
notes: Negative Articles used: Semafor (Houthi missile intercept + diplomatic-isolation framing) and Washington Post/John Hudson via The Spokesman-Review (US intelligence assessment on Saudi nuclear-weapons option). A WSJ-sourced 'Saudi/UAE urge Trump to keep Iran pressure' item was found in-window via Iran International but DROPPED on source-eligibility grounds: Iran International's funding has been publicly linked to Saudi interests, so under SKILL.md's 'when in doubt about ownership, don't use it' rule it was excluded. Saudi named-entity/festival/people/place sweep returned nothing genuinely in-window (National Day activations pre-dated the 25-26 Sep window); Saudi Arabia/Regional content came from the creative-culture-retrieval angle (Jeddah Fashiontex Expo via Bangladeshi trade press; Bahrain-Saudi 'Firdaws 3' exhibition via Bahrain's Al-Bilad). Culture-commission count = 2 (Fashion, Visual Arts), below the WARN target of 3 on a genuinely thin day; not padded. RSS pre-filter feeds that failed to parse this run: HeritageDaily, Arkeonews, The Art Newspaper, Publishers Weekly.
